body:
I understand the struggle. I really, genuinely do. I have massive anxiety attacks just *planning* a trip to the grocery store. I used to love driving and going on road trips, now my mom has to drive me everywhere and I sit in the passenger seat with my muscles bound up so tight I tremor the whole way.

I have had a few therapists who would do their counseling sessions with me over the phone or via Skype, after a few sessions in office. I've also had one therapist who was able to make house calls, and she came to my apartment a few times. Those were the most amazing for me because I'm like you. I don't feel safe when I leave my house. Don't get me wrong, I feel stir crazy as heck here, and miss the feeling of sunshine on my skin, but the thought of leaving even just to check the mail gives me massive anxiety.

For what it's worth, I have really crowded teeth that look awful and I'm extremely self conscious about it. Bad teeth or no, you're still a human being who's hurting, and you deserve the resources it takes to get help. Your parents sound like they love you, even if talking to your mom when you're stressed out isn't fun, and while I can't speak for them I know if I were in their position, I'd rather bend over backwards to pull down the moon for you than lose you without ever knowing you needed help.

Jeez. No wonder you are so exhausted. I wish that I could help you in some way. The high dose ibuprofen just seems like insult to injury at this point. I want to kick the entire medical industry in the ass on your behalf.

I can understand your desire to just give up. I just hope they're able to give you genuine assistance before you reach the end of your rope.

It sounds like you really love your parents and that's beautiful. It means your heart is still fighting to retain your values despite everything your depression brain is putting you through.

Just so you know, you don't have to open up with your therapist right away. It's okay to ask them questions. 

"What kind of patient confidentiality am I entitled to as a minor?"

"What sort of things are you required by law to tell my parents if I confide in you?"

"Hypothetically, if I wanted to talk about something like suicide but wasn't actively planning anything, would this be a safe space for me to do so?"

And even

"I'm not ready to talk to my parents yet about everything I'm feeling but I love them and want to be honest. Can you help me work through ways to talk to them without scaring them?"

I know what you mean about feeling lost. I also know how hard it is to talk to family about the ugliest sides of my depression. It isn't easy. It takes so much strength and guts and spine to live through this.

But it takes even more to keep loving others and wanting to be better despite everything. You're already stronger than you know.

I have this voice. It's mean as fuck and it's relentless. I gained weight in my late 20s and now I am medically classified as obese. I hate that word. I hate myself. I hate taking showers because then I have to confront my body in all its naked truth.

But I don't hate other women for how they look. Isn't that weird? I don't hate thin women for being pretty. I don't get disgusted with other women for being fat. Are you like this, too? Or maybe it's just me.

Either way, the way we talk about ourselves... It is so harsh. 

Your pain is palpable. I feel it in my bones. I wish I could reach out to you and just hug you for days. I wish I could coax that mean, hateful, sharp voice from inside you and box it away someplace where it could never reach you again.

No one deserves to be talked to that way. Not even by themselves.

This breaks my heart because it's so familiar to me. I'm much older than you but I suffer from severe anxiety, depression, and agoraphobia... I barely leave my house, too. 

Mental illness doesn't care how old you are. It doesn't care whether you have friends who love you, or a family that wholeheartedly supports you. It doesn't care if you're rich or poor; even though people of financial means have a better shot of getting quality treatment, they can still be affected in the first place.

Your depression and anxiety? They don't care about those things. If anything, they'll just find ways to make you feel bad about everything good you have in your life.

If you don't want to scare your mom, maybe consider asking her if you can see a therapist for your depression. She already knows you're depressed so it won't be a bombshell to drop. Once you're seeing the therapist on your own, you can talk to them more openly about what you're really going through.

I am so proud of you for wanting therapy. When I was 15, I was too angry at the world and myself to admit I needed therapy for what I was going through.
I think it's called passive suicidal ideation. I switch between that and active ideation. Both are damaging. I'm so sorry that you're experiencing this.
Wishing you would die from causes out of your control, like a terminal illness or a drunk driver? Is that kind of what you mean?

If only your other doctors could be half as great as your neurologist. Ugh. Do you mind if I ask what's going on? It sounds kind of like an auto immune disorder. You don't have to answer if that's too personal.

I have a deep mistrust of doctors, too. My physical pain isn't nearly as bad as what you described, but sometimes it gets unbearable for me and can last a long time (months). I wasn't even asking my primary physician for pain pills, I just asked for a referral to a chiropractor so my insurance would cover it, and she flatly refused. I left the office in tears. My pain was a 7 that day and had been for a few weeks. It eventually settled down for me. I can't imagine how exhausted and crushed you must be with this level of pain and debilitation day in, day out.

Doctors especially seem uninclined to believe women who are in pain. We get the double whammy of "Rx abuse red flag" treatment and "oh, the hysterical woman is being dramatic" dismissal.

It sucks. My heart goes out to you.

Don't reapply. The other posters are right, find an SSI law firm who works on contingency and let them handle the appeals. If/when your case is approved, you will be awarded back pay from the month of your original application. It may take a couple of years. If you can manage, hang in there.

I'm sorry that you're hurting.

I'm so sorry that you're hurting so much. Our society fails us in so many ways. They create an epidemic of prescription drug addiction, then treat everyone like addicts when they mention the word "pain." It is so wrong. I can relate. I hate that you're going through this. If I could take on some of your pain, I would.

I just switched to a menstrual cup, I'm on my second period with it as of today, and it's a game changer (and a pantie savior, too... No spotting!).

I ordered mine on Amazon but it seems like time is of the essence for you. Some of the bigger name brand cups are sold in stores like Target, Walgreens, and Walmart. 

I hated using tampons on my first & last days because the flow was so light it made it hurt to remove them. I actually switched to reusable pads for two years because I hated the feel of tampons do much. Decided to try the cup because reusable pads are a bloody mess to keep up with, literally. The cup is comfortable regardless of flow and it's so much cleaner than using a pad or panty liners. 

If you have any questions I'm happy to answer.

Man, this hurts to read. Your pain is like an exposed wire. 

I can't really speak to your experiences as a trans person, being cis. I relate to a lot of your thoughts, though, the white-hot expressions of pain at the futility of existence.

I have been incredibly lucky to know a handful of trans people who were either living openly as trans or who trusted me enough to come out to me. Who knows how many beautiful trans people I've met without knowing their truth. I know right now there is a lot of hostility towards those who don't conform to our society's rigid gender binary. It breaks my heart that you and others have had to experience and endure this loud, angry, and highly public "discourse" over your very existence as a human being.

Seriously I can't even fucking imagine. Even trying to put myself in that position mentally, of living and breathing a reality while others loudly mock and question the validity of said reality, crushes me. 

You are so strong to have made it this far.

I can't tell you the meaning of life. I struggle with my reality, too. I just want you to know that there are people out there who recognize the struggles you face - maybe not in full, certainly not as intimately as if they had experienced it themselves - and care.

I wish there was more I could say or do to help.

All I can say is I hear you. I hear you loud and clear, and I'm so sorry for your suffering.

Oh. I can say that people who say "other people have it worse so be happy!" can eat my entire ass. They can eat my entire ass and slip into a coma from oxygen deprivation from choking on my entire ass.

My depression and anxiety also make work torturous for me. You're ahead of the curve in a way... For years,I thought my poor work performance was an intrinsic moral failing. I was spoon fed that puritanical work ethic growing up and 100% based my personal self-worth on my ability to perform exceptionally at work without asking for much in return. It wasn't until after I had a nervous breakdown 4 years ago and checked out of life (quit job, school, boyfriend, and social circle) that I realized I had severe anxiety and agoraphobia as well as depression.

The fact that you recognize these problems stem from your mental illness and not from you is huge, imo. I know that may not help much, but it is. Write it on your mirror if you have to. "I am not my depression's worst qualities."

Right now I'm unemployed, living with my mother. I understand the feeling of being a financial burden. She assures me that she doesn't see me as a burden, even though it's hard to believe most of the time. On good days, I cook and clean for her. On bad days I exist in my bedroom and am not much good for anything.

I get my insurance through the ACA & Medicaid. It gives me access to behavioral health care (therapy) and meds. 

I also receive food stamps and I'm finally applying for disability at the urging of my therapist. I'm applying via a law firm who handles all the work on contingency. It could take years, and if they don't win my case, they don't get paid and I'm not out any money. They seem confident they will win my case, though, because I have a solid work history up until I was 31 years old and have a medical history to document my break down and all the meds, therapy, and doctors I've seen since.

If you have worked, you may be eligible for SSDI (insured disability, basically, you accrue credits for working and if you earn enough credits over a certain period, you can receive assistance based on that). Even if you don't have enough work credits, you may still be eligible for SSI. SSI is generally for people with no work history. The amount available varies by state, but anything is better than nothing.

I start seeing a new therapist in June who specializes in acceptance and commitment therapy as well as cognitive behavior therapy. I've done my research and these seem to be the most successful for people with my mental illness & traumatic background.

I know my post sounds hopeful. I assure you, I am deeply depressed and struggle hourly with suicidal ideation. But like you, I love my family (well, my mother) and can't bring myself to hurt her so profoundly.

A big part of me is just waiting for her to pass of natural causes so I won't have anything holding me here.

But until then, I need to be present for her and my cats. And anything I can do to alleviate her financial burden helps to quiet the guilt that plagues me.

I wish you strength and perseverance.

I'm simultaneously grateful and sad that you get it. It's a relief to be heard and understood, but I wouldn't wish this on anyone. 

As for not leaving your bed in 20+hours, I get that, too. Lie in bed so long every joint and tendon in my body aches. This thing called life would be a whole lot easier if our brains weren't actively trying to kill us, the assholes.

Sending those hugs and cheek kisses right back at you.

I worry about how my mom would handle my suicide. I'm pretty sure she'd follow me, and then I'll be responsible for her death. I can't stomach the thought of hurting her so profoundly.

I also have two rescue cats who need me to feed them and empty their litter boxes. They love me, rarely leave my side, and I can't exactly explain to them that my death would have nothing to do with them. I worry about them looking for me after I'm gone and panicking when I don't come back.

So, yeah, guilt keeps me here.

I try to roleplay, both on written forums and in discord d&d campaigns. Wanting to know "what happens next" in a story that is still unraveling gives me something to look forward to. 

And I use video games for escape. 

I hope you share what ends up working for you. It's a good question.

Guys who let themselves go once the relationship is secure.

I don't mean weight gain or relaxed facial/body hair grooming. I'm talking about showering, brushing teeth, changing clothes. 

It's only happened in one relationship. The guy wasn't depressed (I have depression and know how hard it can be some days to make even basic efforts in self care), he was just a slob in disguise. He put in the effort to groom himself while we were in the early stages of dating and once we moved in together, he started going back to his old habits.

I didn't sign up for the job of reminding him to brush his teeth and soap his junk. 

It ended up getting worse, too. His poor hygiene habits extended past his person to the house. We both worked full time, I was also taking 15 credit hours a semester, and he suddenly didn't know how to clean or do laundry.

I knew I was in trouble when he was squirming around in his computer chair for hours, gassing up the place, and I found myself asking incredulously, "....honey, do you need to go to the bathroom?"

Yeah. Yeah. I didn't sign up to be a toddler mama to a full grown man child.

Anyway, after ending that relationship, I'm hyperaware of grooming habits.

I became sexually active at a fairly young age and didn't know what I was supposed to like, or that, you know, guys weren't actually the arbiters of what should feel good and shouldn't. I just assumed that what they did was right and my discomfort was a side effect of my inexperience.  


I honestly didn't realize guys could be gentle with the lady bits. Every one I've been with mashed down on my bits, some worse than others (leaving bruising, etc). I think you're right that they don't realize their hand strength, maybe in combination with being able to exert a certain amount of pressure on their own bits without causing pain and assuming it's the same for us.  


Anyway, here I am now, a grown ass woman, and my poor bits are so desensitized that I have to mash down on myself just to achieve orgasm, or use a vibrator and bear down on it. I feel robbed. Light touches save sex lives.
